newsitem.title: GERMANY: Nervous German DAX ends bourse down 1.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Nervous German DAX ends bourse down 1.7 pct.

text.p: Worries about a possible delay for Europe's monetary union and the fate of U.S. interest rates pushed German shares down to a two-week low in a choppy bourse session on Tuesday.
The DAX lost 59.80 points, or 1.8 percent, to end bourse trade at 3,291.19 points, dropping below the psychologically crucial 3,300-point level for the first time since early March.
Added to EMU and U.S. worries came pressure associated with the expiry later this week of options on the DAX.
"It's been everything together today," said one Frankfurt dealer. "The options expiry seems to be playing havoc with pricing and we need some convincing reassurance from the U.S."

Volumes were relatively moderate with market attention fixed on steelmaker Thyssen, whose shares were suspended from official trade amid widespread expectation that rival firm Krupp was poised to launch a takeover bid.

The news raised a storm on the German market, where hostile takeovers are rare, and sent Thyssen shares soaring to an all-time high of 400 marks in unofficial trading -- the so-called grey market. The shares had closed late trade on Monday at 344.50 marks.
Rumours were flying that Krupp would offer up to 450 marks per share to small Thyssen shareholders.
"The Thyssen story is the only one people want to hear about today," commented one trader. "If they were trading, we could have a different story here."
Rival engineering firm Preussag also got a boost from the takeover talk as dealers speculated that a merger would cut capacity in the sector. Preussag rose 7.70 marks to 437.70 marks.

The chemical sector was weak after Bayer said it would struggle to surpass 1996 profits this year. BASF also ended lower, despite getting a brief boost from 1996 sales and earnings data that were slightly ahead of forecast.
Nonetheless, dealers noted that Germany's big three chemical companies -- which also include Hoechst -- were coming increasingly close on price.
Where previously Hoechst led Bayer, with BASF trailing a very poor third, Bayer ended at 68.70 marks on Tuesday, Hoechst was at 67.05 marks and BASF was at 61.51 marks.
